nodes.name: WF1 Trigger
nodes.notes: This node's Production URL is what you paste into WF1's Config node as wf2WebhookUrl once this workflow is activated. responseMode=onReceived acks WF1 immediately rather than making it wait for the whole batch of emails to send.

nodes.name: Config - Fill In After Import
nodes.notes: sheetDocumentId must be the SAME Google Sheet as WF1's Config node - copy the value across. All placeholder REPLACE_WITH_... values must be filled in before running. These stay inside n8n's own storage, never shared elsewhere.

nodes.name: Read Master Sheet
nodes.notes: Reads all rows to find guests needing their first payment email and to collect every existing Ticket Number for uniqueness checking. Requires the same Google Sheets OAuth2 credential as WF1.

nodes.name: Filter Rows Needing First Email
nodes.notes: A guest is due a first email once: Status is Pending AND conversationId is still blank. _existingTicketNumbers rides along on every row so the grouping step downstream can generate a Ticket Number that's guaranteed not to collide with one already in the sheet.

nodes.name: Filter Bills Having PDF
nodes.notes: TRUE (fileId present, the normal case since WF1's Apps Script step already populated it) = download the PDF to attach. FALSE (fileId still blank) = skip download, that bill just won't have an attachment in the first email rather than erroring the whole batch.

nodes.name: Loop Bills for PDF Download
nodes.notes: One Drive download per bill needing an invoice PDF attached. Output 0 = done, output 1 = current batch.

nodes.name: Download Invoice PDF
nodes.notes: Uses the same Google OAuth2 credential as WF1's Drive nodes.

nodes.name: Combine Bill and Binary
nodes.notes: Google Drive's download operation outputs the file under binary property 'data' by default - verify this against your n8n version. Renames it to 'file' for a consistent downstream key.

nodes.name: Merge PDF Download Paths
nodes.notes: Waits for BOTH the bills that had no fileId (Filter's false branch) and the bills that just finished the PDF download loop (Loop's done output) before continuing, and concatenates them into one flat list. Same reasoning as WF1's Merge PDF Lookup Paths node - without this, Group Bills into Email Threads fires before the loop branch has a chance to run.

nodes.name: Group Bills into Email Threads
nodes.notes: Groups by customer_id+guest_name - same thread key WF1 uses - so a guest with several bills (Single or Consolidate) gets ONE combined first email listing every bill, matching the 'Submission of Invoices' template's per-bill summary table. Generates one unique 8-digit Ticket Number per thread, checked against every ticket number already in the sheet plus ones just generated in this same run. Re-keys each bill's downloaded PDF binary onto the group item as attachment_0, attachment_1, ... for the Outlook node to reference.

nodes.name: Loop Email Threads
nodes.notes: One first-payment email per guest thread. Output 0 = done, output 1 = current batch.

nodes.name: Build Email Content
nodes.notes: Builds subject/body from the 'Submission of Invoices & Payment Link' template text supplied 2026-07-20, with a per-bill summary table and a signature built dynamically from the sheet's cse_name/cse_email_id columns (placeholder designation text - swap in a real signature block/logo once one exists). Subject carries [Ref: <ticketNumber>] for WF4's regex fallback matching.

nodes.name: Record Send Result
nodes.notes: SMTP has no Graph-style conversationId, so this repurposes the two columns: conversationId becomes the ROOT Message-ID (stays fixed for the life of the thread, and is what Filter Rows Needing First Email checks to know a first email already went out), Message ID becomes the MOST RECENT Message-ID (for WF3 to set In-Reply-To/References against when it replies, so mail clients still thread the conversation visually via RFC 822 headers instead of a Graph conversationId). sendResult.messageId is nodemailer's generated Message-ID, exposed by n8n's Email Send node - verify the exact output field name in your version. Merges it back onto the full thread (with its bills array) before looping back, so Loop Email Threads' done output carries the enriched data - same technique WF1 uses to get enriched task data out of Loop Invoice Tasks' done output.

nodes.name: Wait 1s (SMTP)
nodes.notes: Throttle protection between sends.

nodes.name: Expand Threads to Bill Rows
nodes.notes: Runs once, on the 'done' output of Loop Email Threads. Flattens each thread back into one row per bill_no. Only these 5 columns are sent to the sheet on purpose - Status and every other column are left as WF1 already wrote them, relying on appendOrUpdate's partial-column-update behaviour (verify this against a real row before trusting it).

nodes.name: Update Master Sheet
nodes.notes: Matches existing rows by bill_no (already present from WF1) and updates just Ticket Number, conversationId, Message ID and Last Updated on each.

nodes.name: Send Email (SMTP) - AI Automation
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN THE N8N UI: exact field names for the installed Email Send (SMTP) node version - 'emailFormat'/'html' and the attachments option shape are a best guess since this can't be checked without live access. Requires an SMTP credential attached (host/port/user/password) - attach after import, same as WF1's Google OAuth2 credentials. IMPORTANT: if the sending mailbox is on Microsoft 365/Exchange Online, confirm SMTP AUTH (Basic Auth) is actually enabled for this mailbox first - Microsoft has been disabling it tenant-wide by default since 2022, and if it's off this node will fail outright with an auth error, not a silent issue. If SMTP AUTH can't be turned on, use a relay (SendGrid/Amazon SES/etc.) instead of connecting directly to smtp.office365.com.
